Needs changes before merge.

The alias fix passes its regression tests. One required heavy test fails on Linux x86_64.
The same failure occurs on upstream main. This review does not attribute that failure to this PR.
AGENTS.md, "Heavy lanes at review", requires a green result for each reached heavy lane.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144` and `:191`: resolve the failed Linux path reading before this PR becomes ready.
   `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` gives `(3158, 3130, 1141)`.
   The Linux assertion expects `(4726, 4698, 549)`.
   The verification, budget, and fallback assertions before this assertion pass.
   The failure repeats on this head and on upstream main `0306743decfa53783235780eb33b578052dfd6de`.
   Explain the changed path before updating an expected value. Provide a green result for the reached heavy lanes.

Failure output:

```text
thread 'the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean' panicked at crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144:5:
the bore's path as the fix plans it: (3158, 3130, 1141)
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2 filtered out
```

Checks:

- All builds and tests ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2927`. No GitHub runner was used.
- The full gate tree contained upstream main `3ffe2338f775b2f254524f5f8e642aae5181aebb`. This head already contained that commit.
- Upstream main advanced during the gate. A later trial merge with `0306743decfa53783235780eb33b578052dfd6de` was clean. All five scale tests passed on that merged tree.
  The same heavy test failed there with the same counts.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 80 steps passed; 1743 tests passed; 33 tests ignored; 19.3 minutes.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 249 steps; 248 passed; one failed; 47.6 minutes.
  The kernel and motion lanes passed. The app lane has the failure above.
  Nine known-fail checks failed at their expected assertions and passed the gate checks.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The ISO registry confirms `GUAC` and `SUNT`: [ISO short names](https://standards.iso.org/iso/10303/tech/short_names/short-names.txt).
- The parsed records are canonical before validation and topology read. Strings, references, and parameters are unchanged.
- Both new STEP fixtures have explicit rows in `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`.
- No existing golden moved. I checked both new corpus rows against their fixture units and comparison paths.
  Their raw tessellator and truck differences are explicit. The scale tests check the imported dimensions and volume.
- No UI, dependency, workflow, or process file changed. No screenshot is required for this diff.

Mutations, run independently by this reviewer:

| Mutation | Red result | Restored result |
|---|---|---|
| Remove `GUAC` mapping | `short_context_only_import_keeps_scale` fails | passes |
| Remove `SUNT` mapping | `short_si_unit_only_import_keeps_scale` fails | passes |

Both mutations were temporary. All five scale tests passed again after restoration.

Extra suites run:

- Explicit `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement`: 24 passed.
- Explicit `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test machining_mesh`: 7 passed.
- Explicit `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join`: 4 passed; one known-fail test handled by the heavy gate.

- `step_short_units` passed all five tests. The full STEP agreement suite passed all 24 tests, including both new fixtures.
- The Linux failure is a base-tree validation blocker. No new code defect was found in the alias change.
- `solidcore_step.rs` now has 404 lines. `step_agreement.rs` was already above the approximate file limit. This is not blocking.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: The Linux bore path assertion and the reached heavy-lane blocker from the latest review.

PR #2904 (`bac4a96c7`) replaced the truck STEP reader with solidcore. The same fixture now imports with 6228 facets, instead of 952. Decision #917 records this mesh change. The fixture and the relevant HSM planner files are unchanged across that switch. The planner derives its level regions and proved arc fits from the mesh.

Updated the measured Linux tuple to `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. Extended `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` to pin the imported mesh and cutting levels `[0, 5, 10, 15]`. The verification, budget, and fallback assertions remain in place.

Evidence:

- The original tuple failed with the reported actual tuple.
- Restoring the old tuple failed again. Restoring the fix passed.
- Mutating the facet expectation to 952 failed. Restoring it passed.
- Adding the Z20 air level to the expected levels failed. Restoring it passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: all 80 steps passed; 1743 tests passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: all 249 steps passed. The kernel, motion, and app lanes passed. All nine known-fail checks matched their expected failures.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

All gates ran on unchanged head `4cafca282fc48cb73c1a847e5cf6c7e04d4f0576`.

Please re-review this head.
